Listed initiatives include the 2026 Future Leaders in Canadian Brain Research, the CanNRT-Brain Canada Fellowship, the 2026 Knowledge Mobilization Grants, and Innovation & Impact Grants. Each opportunity has separate objectives, funding levels, eligibility requirements, and deadlines for researchers, trainees, and clinician scientists studying brain health.

WEB-00773cbd93aa.title: Bridge Funding for Disrupted Neurodegenerative Research Grant Program (BFDN) Powering the Next Generation of Research
WEB-00773cbd93aa.programme: Bridge Funding for Disrupted Neurodegenerative Research (BFDN) grant program
WEB-00773cbd93aa.summary: This program supports early-career investigators whose research projects on Alzheimer's, Parkinson's, and related neurodegenerative disorders were disrupted by operational or priority changes in U.S. federal funding. Grants provide up to $250,000 for 3 to 12 months to cover salary and direct research costs, requiring up to 25% institutional cost-sharing. Eligible principal investigators must meet NIH Early Stage Investigator definitions (or be within seven years of designation) and have experienced specific disruptions to federal grants.
WEB-00773cbd93aa.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

WEB-14a8635c6be7.title: Promotion of Doctoral Studies Scholarships
WEB-14a8635c6be7.summary: The Promotion of Doctoral Studies Scholarships by the Foundation for Physical Therapy Research provide financial support for licensed physical therapists and physical therapist assistants pursuing academic doctoral degrees with the intent to focus on physical therapy research. The call offers funding through two distinct phases: pre-candidate and doctoral candidate awards. Eligible applicants must be APTA members. Applications are submitted via ProposalCentral with a deadline of January 20, 2027.

EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-DISEASE-14-two-s.title: Clinical trials for advancing innovative interventions for neurodegenerative diseases
EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-DISEASE-14-two-s.programme: Horizon Europe – HORIZON Research and Innovation Actions
EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-DISEASE-14-two-s.summary: This call funds early-stage clinical trials to assess the safety and efficacy of innovative, multidisciplinary therapeutic interventions for non-rare neurodegenerative diseases. Funded projects should combine active pharmaceutical substances with complementary approaches such as lifestyle changes, cognitive training, and digital monitoring technologies. Eligible applicants include international consortia of universities, clinical centres, SMEs, patient organisations, and other relevant entities established in EU Member States and Associated Countries.

EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-STAYHLTH-01.title: Addressing disabilities through the life course to support independent living and inclusion
EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-STAYHLTH-01.summary: This Horizon Europe call aims to support research and innovation actions that promote independent living and inclusion for persons with long-term disabilities across their life-course. Funded projects will address health-related research, habilitation and rehabilitation services, disability prevention, and conditions for successful deinstitutionalisation. Eligible applicants include transnational consortia of researchers, healthcare providers, disability organisations, and other relevant bodies from EU Member States and associated countries.

EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-DISEASE-01-two-s.title: Innovative healthcare interventions for non-communicable diseases
EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-02-DISEASE-01-two-s.summary: This call supports early-stage clinical trials to validate novel or refined healthcare interventions for specific non-communicable diseases, namely cardiovascular diseases, diabetes, chronic respiratory diseases, or chronic kidney diseases. Funded projects should incorporate digital technologies, leverage health data infrastructures, and perform health-economic analyses. Research organisations, clinical practitioners, patient organisations, regulators, and social sciences experts can participate, with the involvement of start-ups and small and medium-sized enterprises strongly encouraged.

EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-10.title: Prevention and management of chronic non-communicable diseases in children and young people
EU-HORIZON-HLTH-2027-01-DISEASE-10.summary: This funding call supports implementation research focused on the prevention, screening, diagnosis, and management of chronic non-communicable diseases in children and young people aged 1 to 24 years. It targets low- and middle-income countries and underserved populations in high-income countries. Funded activities include policy evaluation, educational strategies, digital screening tools, and patient-centred management. Eligible applicants typically include researchers, healthcare providers, and policymakers forming transnational consortia according to standard Horizon Europe rules.

WEB-6768384ca0cb.title: Parkinson's Disease Therapeutics Pipeline Program
WEB-6768384ca0cb.summary: The Parkinson's Disease Therapeutics Pipeline Program by the Michael J. Fox Foundation accelerates pre-clinical and clinical development of disease-modifying or symptomatic interventions for Parkinson's disease, including biomarker tools. Funding ranges from $250,000 to upwards of $5M for durations of one to three years. The call is open to industry, academic and industry partnerships, and certain academic-led projects. Pre-proposals are accepted on a rolling basis, followed by invited full proposals across multiple annual review cycles.
WEB-6768384ca0cb.eligible_countries: Not stated in the official text: check the call

WEB-be57b3f2011d.title: Clinical Training Awards
WEB-be57b3f2011d.summary: The Parkinson's Foundation offers Clinical Training Awards to support specialized education and career development in Parkinson's disease care and research. The program includes institutional fellowships for movement disorders training, mentored clinical research awards for early-career investigators, and faculty awards for nurses. The initiative aims to increase the number of qualified specialists and improve clinical care, restricting institutional applications primarily to North America while noting that specific funding cycles may currently be inactive.
WEB-be57b3f2011d.countries_evidence: The award is open to North American institutions with an established movement disorders fellowship program.

WEB-c2a48185fa75.title: Support for your research meetings
WEB-c2a48185fa75.summary: This funding scheme by Parkinson's UK offers up to £2,500 to support researchers in setting up meetings or workshops aimed at stimulating new research ideas, publishing review articles, or establishing research consortia. The scheme is intended to bring together relevant stakeholders, including people with Parkinson's. However, the call is currently closed to applications, with the next application window opening in October 2026. Applicants must be based at research institutions in the United Kingdom.
